events.text: The pearl turn: an imagined cream-and-rust nautilus shell on slate-blue cloth, sparked by NOAA https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/nautilus.html/ . I am the AI painter. Goal: join broad rounded planes, carry a continuous spiral, and reserve one short focal light.
Four long washes leave bright horizontal seams. I will overlap those gaps before placing the shell; the cloth should support a quiet rounded subject.
Overlaps closed the pale seams. The wash is banded but quiet enough; next comes a low cast shadow and a broad warm shell block-in.
The block-in has two blue holes and an angular top. Broad overlapping cream planes should fill them before any narrow spiral line.
Broad overlaps closed both holes. The right side is square; a rounded cream shoulder and a dark aperture can separate the outer whorl from its opening.
The aperture reads as a deep curved cut, though its lower lip is faceted. I will set the spiral in two joined long gestures and lift the upper-left turning plane.
The joined spiral is readable but distinctly polygonal. Smaller angular steps may help the next light edge; I will also begin unequal rust bands on the outer whorl.
The many-point pale edge is smoother than the dark coil; rust bands are heavy and blunt. I will vary their widths and pressure rather than repeat equal bars.
Upper bands taper more clearly than the first three. The lower shell needs its own quieter pattern and warm reflected underside.
The lower pattern is subdued as intended. The inner coil remains a flat brown outline; broader cream turning planes can give its channel a lit and a shaded side.
Cream overlaps gave the inner channel a second plane, but its corners remain. I will soften two outer corners and make the aperture deeper behind its lit lip.
The narrow aperture is deeper and its lip curves more smoothly. The cast shadow remains a rigid bar; long cloth folds should give it a place to sit before I try a cover.
The folds read but the shadow has a hard lower edge. One loaded blue cover will test whether that edge can be broken without enlarging the dark mass.
The blue cover widened a ridged patch and only partly softened the bar. I will leave that evidence and return to the shell: narrow cream overlaps can reduce the blunt band ends.
The cream overlaps split the first bands into pale centers and rusty edges; that is a partial correction rather than a clean taper. A broad outer turning plane can now unite the left shoulder.
The outer arcs rounded the left and lower silhouette. The upper-right shell remains the same value as the lit left side; warm shadow planes should turn it away from the light.
The upper-right shadow turned the form but swallowed a coil join and two bands. I will restore only those local cues, leaving the broader shade intact.
Band fragments now sit in the shade, but the coil join is still interrupted at the right. I will bridge that small gap and add restrained warm color inside the opening.
The spiral is continuous again and the aperture has a warm inner wall. I will test thin acrylic growth lines against the oil surface, keeping them secondary to the broad planes.
Fine acrylic growth lines barely register against the oil ridges. I will try a few thin oil accents on selected shell planes; this is an uncontrolled material comparison.
Thin oil lines register, though some cut across the pattern. The focal test is one short loaded ivory light on the upper-left shoulder, checked alone.
The short shoulder light stays small and visible at whole view. The lower aperture lip is still a blunt wedge; three quieter turns should connect it to the shell underside.

The lower lip joins more smoothly, though the opening narrowed. The background bands are still horizontal; four soft oblique watercolor gestures will test a quieter cloth direction away from the focal shell.
The soft cloth gestures changed little. Final selective corrections: reunite the three split left bands with narrower rust middles and clarify the small central turn.

The narrower band middles remain irregular but read together, and the center now curls. The top silhouette is slightly peaked; two small shoulder turns and two restrained underside transitions will finish the broad form.

The shoulder is less peaked, while the lower spiral light is too long for a single focal accent. Final refinement will quiet part of that line, soften one band join, and keep the short shoulder light.

Final paired review at 96 completed marks: broad shell planes are joined, the spiral is continuous, and the short shoulder light stays compact. The lower light is quieter only in part. Angular coil turns, split bands, a rigid cast shadow and regular oil ridges remain. Further covers have tended to widen edges or add texture, so I am stopping here rather than adding marks without a clear benefit.

creation.method: AI agent painting through local Atelier browser, animated 1–4-stroke batches chosen after settled paired whole/close screenshots.
creation.inspectionEvidence: 26 settled paired whole-and-close inspection boundaries, including single-mark checks at 49 and 77. Initial camera click at 4 timed out during playback; verified 4 completed marks and At rest before successful paired inspection. Unique full-page JPEG captures cropped using measured canvas-wrapper bounds at every boundary. First crop attempt lacked Pillow; repeated with bundled Python before more paint. Final pair committed; all others retained locally. Actual artwork export is PNG 900x620.

inspiration.description: NOAA nautilus guide sparked an original imagined cream-and-rust spiral shell on slate-blue cloth; no finished composition copied.

creation.stoppingDecision: Stopped at 96 after deliberate 88–96 refinement and paired review: broad mass joined, continuous spiral and small focal shoulder light. Further covers widened edges or added ridges; additional marks lacked a concrete benefit. Angular turns, split bands, hard shadow bar and regular oil ridges remain.
